**Group:** Zooplankton  ·  **Optics:** high-mag, low-mag

## Defining characteristics

A larvacean (appendicularian): a small planktonic tunicate with a trunk and a long muscular tail, giving a tadpole-like shape, frequently enclosed in a transparent gelatinous mucous house used to filter food. Discarded houses are also common in imagery. Key features: tadpole body (trunk plus tail), often a surrounding mucous house.

## Distinguishing from similar classes

| Similar class | How to tell them apart |
|---|---|
| **ctenophora** | Ctenophores are large ovoid/lobed comb jellies; larvaceans are small tadpole-shaped animals, often in a mucous house. |
| **aggregate** | A discarded larvacean house can resemble an aggregate, but shows the structured chambers of a feeding house rather than a random floc. |
